svg.title: More conventional current enters than leaves, so electrons are lost
svg.desc: A fixed control volume receives conventional current I_left=2 microampere from the left and sends I_right=1 microampere to the right. The blue arrows both point right; the gold net-electron-flow arrows both point left. Individual electrons can move in either direction; these arrows show the mean imbalance. Arrow lengths indicate direction only, not magnitudes. The enclosed budget after one nanosecond is Delta Q=+1 femtocoulomb and Delta N_e about minus 6242. The fixed positive background does not change. Hence an increase of net positive charge is a loss of electrons, not a source of new charge. Boundary currents are prescribed; this is not a self-consistent electrostatic solution.
svg.text: Conventional current and net electron flow have opposite signs

ns0:svg.data-latex: \Delta Q=(I_{\rm left}-I_{\rm right})\Delta t,\qquad\Delta N_e=-\Delta Q/e,\quad e>0

svg.text: Fixed positive background · mean values · arrows show direction, not magnitude
